newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK TO FOCUS ON DOMESTIC SALES, PLASTICS.
newsitem.headline: TVK TO FOCUS ON DOMESTIC SALES, PLASTICS.

text.p: Hungarian chemical company Tiszai Vegyi Kombinat (TVK) said it plans to trim overseas exports and make plastics processing its main prority.

"We plan to develop plastics processing as the driving force (within TVK's production)," TVK's general director CEO Miklos Varhegyi told Reuters following a news conference on Thursday. "We have some plastics processing projects in an advanced stage."
Varszegy said he could not elaborate because of "fierce competition within the (plastics processing) market".

He also said the overhaul of its olefins plant would be completed as planned in 1997 and the German contractor's recent study showed that output could be increased thereafter by as much as 20 to 25 percent.
Varhegyi said the company plans to reduce poliethylene (PE) and polipropylene (PP) overseas exports to traditional customers due to high transport costs and expectations of growing European demand.
"Ethylene shortage will be a defining feature of the petrochemicals industry in the coming years," he said.
He added that TVK will continue to rely on west European exports as the domestic market alone would not take up their entire production.
However, TVK also expects domestic plastics processing to grow faster than in western Europe.
"Our main customer base, the packaging industry is expanding," he said, adding that an increasing number of multinationals are starting plastics processing in Hungary.
He said the company plans to increase the proportion of domestic sales by an annual one to three percent over the next years.
TVK's exports amount to some 60 percent of sales.
On the domestic market, TVK has a 65 percent share in poliethylene and 80 percent in polipropylene, he said.
Varhegyi said recent sharp gains in TVK shares, introduced to the Budapest Stock Exchange in August, had shown that the stocks had woken up from their dormant state in November.
"I attribute the rise to three factors: third quarter results, analysts' ratings and the news about the local government share package," he said.
On the Budapest Stcok Exchange, TVK shares closed at 1,845 forints, up 15.
